scope:
Native continuations of a fixed historical measurement-failure checkpoint.

The four selectors were frozen by an offline screen using the SAME recorded
public measurements and pre-calibration task feedback. This script recreates
the historical physical state by replaying its exact action prefix in a fresh
native world, then executes the frozen predictions. Fresh radiation noise is
logged but does not replace the fixed historical evidence supplied to selectors.
No hypothetical edited reading is presented as a real measurement.

This is a causal continuation comparison on ONE selected development failure,
not four independent worlds, an autonomous learner, or held-out generalization.
All replay and continuation actions are counted separately and in total.

public_task_progress.description: You are at the Quantum Reactor Lab on Planet X. Quantum Crystals offer the potential to generate a great deal of power, but require their respective crystal reactors to be tuned to a specific frequency that appears unique for each crystal. Through great effort, a previous research scientist manually stumbled upon the correct frequencies for Crystal 1, Crystal 2, and Crystal 3, which are in their respective reactors. Your task is to use science to figure out the correct frequency for Crystal 4 and Crystal 5, set their reactors to the appropriate frequency, and install the crystals. Once all four crystals are installed, the reactor will be able to generate a great deal of power. To support your task, a number of scientific instruments are available in the lab.
